title: Two fibres of a smooth-parameter line family have a projective-curve realization
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $Z$ be a smooth separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $S$ be a nonempty smooth connected separated finite-type $k$-scheme. Connected means its underlying topological space is not the disjoint union of two nonempty open subsets; separated means its diagonal is a closed immersion. Let $s_0,s_1\in S(k)$ [def-pc-rational-point] and let $L$ be an invertible module on $Z\times_k S$ [def-sc-invertible-module, def-pc-fibre-product]. There exist a smooth projective geometrically integral curve $C/k$ [def-pc-smooth-projective-curve, def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], points $a,b\in C(k)$, and an invertible module $E$ on $Z\times_k C$ such that $E_a\cong L_{s_0}$ and $E_b\cong L_{s_1}$. Fibres mean tensor pullbacks [def-pc-module-pullback]. The points $a,b$ need not be distinct. No properness, integrality, affineness, or dimension bound on $Z$ is assumed.

source.place: Corollary 1.9, printed p.4, for a curve through the two parameter points, followed by normalization and completion as in Milne, Abelian Varieties, Chapter I Lemma 3.5 (printed p.18). Extension on the smooth product uses Stacks Tag 0BD9, divisors.tex lemma-extend-invertible-module, and regular-local factoriality (more-algebra.tex lemma-regular-local-UFD). This is an agent-assembled consequence, not a claim that Corollary 1.9 states the whole assertion.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular], $S$ is regular. Its assumed nonemptiness and connectedness therefore make it integral by [lem-sc-regular-connected-integral]. Apply [lem-sfb-integral-variety-smooth-curve-interpolation] to $X=S$ and the nonempty finite set $F=\{s_0,s_1\}$. Obtain a smooth separated connected curve $D$, a morphism $g:D\to S$, and $d_0,d_1\in D(k)$ with $g(d_i)=s_i$. When the two given points agree, use the same chosen lift twice. By [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor](1), $M=(\operatorname{id}_Z\times g)^*L$ is invertible on $Z\times_kD$.

source.place: Corollary 1.9, printed p.4; parameter restriction, assembled with Stacks 056S (varieties.tex lemma-smooth-regular), 01ON (properties.tex lemma-characterize-integral), and 0B8L (modules.tex lemma-pullback-invertible).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-compactification] to $D$: there is an open immersion $j:D\hookrightarrow C$ into a smooth proper connected curve $C/k$. Put $a=j(d_0)$ and $b=j(d_1)$. To verify projectivity rather than only properness, [lem-sc-curves-quasi-projective] gives a locally closed immersion $i:C\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_k$. The target is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-proj-separated]. Since $C$ is proper over $k$, [lem-weil-pbc-proper-to-separated] makes $i$ proper, and [lem-weil-pbc-proper-immersion-closed] makes $i$ a closed immersion. Thus $C$ is projective over $k$.

source.place: Chapter I, Lemma 3.5(a), printed p.18; projectivity checked using Stacks 0A25 (varieties.tex lemma-dim-1-quasi-projective), 01NH (constructions.tex lemma-projective-space-separated), and 01IQ (schemes.tex lemma-immersion-when-closed).

proof.text: The algebraic-closure criterion [lem-weil-geometrically-connected-algebraic-closure], applied with $\bar k=k$, makes the nonempty connected $C$ geometrically connected. Smoothness makes it geometrically normal by [lem-trf-smooth-geometrically-normal]. It is of finite type over $k$, so [lem-trf-geonormal-geoconnected-finite-type-integral] makes $C$ geometrically integral. Together with step 2 and $\dim C=1$, these are all the required properties of the parameter curve.

source.place: Tags 0387 (lemma-characterize-geometrically-connected), 056T (lemma-smooth-geometrically-normal); connected-normal integrality on field base changes is properties.tex Tag 033M (lemma-normal-Noetherian).

proof.text: Put $Y=Z\times_kC$ and $U=Z\times_kD$. The map $u=\operatorname{id}_Z\times j:U\to Y$ is an open immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change], since its square with $j$ and $Y\to C$ is cartesian by the product universal property. By [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2), $Y\to C$ is smooth, and [lem-trf-smooth-composition] makes $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ smooth. Consequently [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular] says that $Y$ is locally Noetherian and every local ring is regular local. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-localization], each regular local ring is a regular ring in the sense required by [lem-trf-regular-local-ufd-boundary-factorization]. Applying that node with the empty parameter list ($r=0$) to each local ring shows that it is a UFD. In particular this holds on $Y\setminus U$. Now [lem-sfb-invertible-extension-factorial-complement], applied to the invertible module $M$ on $U$, gives an invertible module $E$ on $Y$ with $u^*E\cong M$. This does not require $Y$ to be integral or connected.

source.place: Tag 0BD9 (lemma-extend-invertible-module); regular local factoriality is more-algebra.tex Tag 0AG0 (lemma-regular-local-UFD); smoothness is morphisms.tex 01VA (lemma-composition-smooth), 01VB (lemma-base-change-smooth), and varieties.tex 056S.

proof.text: For $i=0,1$ let $v_i:Z\to U$ be $z\mapsto(z,d_i)$ and let $w_i:Z\to Z\times_kS$ be $z\mapsto(z,s_i)$. Then $(\operatorname{id}_Z\times g)\circ v_i=w_i$, while $u\circ v_0$ and $u\circ v_1$ are the fibre inclusions at $a$ and $b$. The composition isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor](2), applied to the actual maps, gives $E_a\cong v_0^*u^*E\cong v_0^*M\cong w_0^*L=L_{s_0}$ and $E_b\cong v_1^*u^*E\cong v_1^*M\cong w_1^*L=L_{s_1}$. These identities also apply if $a=b$ or $Z$ is empty.
